req.title: Session cookie has HttpOnly attribute
req.statement: The system shall set HttpOnly on the session cookie.

doc.reasoning: The requirement mandates that the session cookie carries the HttpOnly attribute. Flask sets the session cookie on any response that modifies the session (e.g., a successful login). We test: (1) positive – after a successful POST /auth/login the Set-Cookie header contains 'HttpOnly'; (2) negative – a plain GET to a public page that never touches the session should not emit a Set-Cookie header at all, confirming the attribute is tied to session creation and not spuriously absent; (3) boundary – the HttpOnly flag must be present as a standalone token (case-insensitive, exact token), not merely a substring of another attribute name, catching mutations that remove or rename the flag; (4) state-transition – after logout the session cookie is cleared and the replacement cookie still carries HttpOnly. Each test is self-contained, uses in-process app.test_client(), and asserts exact values to maximise mutation kill rate.

tests.name: test_session_cookie_has_httponly_after_login
preconditions: App is created with TESTING=True and a fresh temp database
User 'Rahul' with password 'stone' exists in the pre-loaded dataset
actions: POST /auth/login with valid credentials username=Rahul password=stone
trace: R-FLASKR-043: session cookie must have HttpOnly attribute
tests.executable:
import tempfile, os
from flaskr import create_app

def test_session_cookie_has_httponly_after_login():
    fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp()
    os.close(fd)
    app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
    with app.app_context():
        from flaskr.db import init_db
        init_db()
    client = app.test_client()
    r = client.post('/auth/login', data={'username': 'Rahul', 'password': 'stone'})
    assert r.status_code == 302
    set_cookie = r.headers.get('Set-Cookie', '')
    assert set_cookie != '', 'Set-Cookie header must be present after login'
    assert 'session' in set_cookie, 'Cookie name must be session'
    directives = [d.strip() for d in set_cookie.split(';')]
    httponly_present = any(d.lower() == 'httponly' for d in directives)
    assert httponly_present, f'HttpOnly directive missing in Set-Cookie: {set_cookie}'

test_session_cookie_has_httponly_after_login()

tests.name: test_no_set_cookie_on_public_get_without_session
preconditions: App is created with TESTING=True and a fresh temp database
No prior session exists; client makes a plain GET to a public endpoint
actions: GET /hello (public route that never touches the session)
expected: No Set-Cookie header is emitted (session was not modified)
trace: R-FLASKR-043: HttpOnly is only relevant when a session cookie is actually set; a route that never writes to the session must not emit Set-Cookie
tests.executable:
import tempfile, os
from flaskr import create_app

def test_no_set_cookie_on_public_get_without_session():
    fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp()
    os.close(fd)
    app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
    with app.app_context():
        from flaskr.db import init_db
        init_db()
    client = app.test_client()
    r = client.get('/hello')
    assert r.status_code == 200
    assert r.data == b'Hello, World!'
    set_cookie = r.headers.get('Set-Cookie', '')
    assert set_cookie == '', f'Unexpected Set-Cookie on public GET: {set_cookie}'

test_no_set_cookie_on_public_get_without_session()

tests.name: test_httponly_is_exact_standalone_directive_not_substring
preconditions: App is created with TESTING=True and a fresh temp database
User 'Anjali' with password 'cloud' exists in the pre-loaded dataset
actions: POST /auth/login with valid credentials username=Anjali password=cloud
Check each directive token individually for exact case-insensitive equality to 'httponly'
expected: No directive is a superset string like 'HttpOnly=true' or 'NotHttpOnly'
trace: R-FLASKR-043: HttpOnly must appear as a standalone boolean flag, not as part of another attribute name or value
tests.executable:
import tempfile, os
from flaskr import create_app

def test_httponly_is_exact_standalone_directive_not_substring():
    fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp()
    os.close(fd)
    app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
    with app.app_context():
        from flaskr.db import init_db
        init_db()
    client = app.test_client()
    r = client.post('/auth/login', data={'username': 'Anjali', 'password': 'cloud'})
    assert r.status_code == 302
    set_cookie = r.headers.get('Set-Cookie', '')
    assert set_cookie != '', 'Set-Cookie header must be present'
    directives = [d.strip() for d in set_cookie.split(';')]
    exact_matches = [d for d in directives if d.lower() == 'httponly']
    assert len(exact_matches) == 1, (
        f'Expected exactly 1 HttpOnly directive, got {exact_matches} in: {set_cookie}'
    )
    spurious = [d for d in directives if 'httponly' in d.lower() and d.lower() != 'httponly']
    assert spurious == [], f'Spurious HttpOnly-containing directives found: {spurious}'

test_httponly_is_exact_standalone_directive_not_substring()

tests.name: test_session_cookie_httponly_persists_after_logout_and_re_login
preconditions: App is created with TESTING=True and a fresh temp database
User 'Ishaan' with password 'stone' exists in the pre-loaded dataset
actions: Assert HttpOnly present on login Set-Cookie
Assert HttpOnly present on the second login Set-Cookie
expected: First login returns 302 with HttpOnly in Set-Cookie
Second login returns 302 with HttpOnly in Set-Cookie
HttpOnly is present in both session-creation responses
trace: R-FLASKR-043: HttpOnly must be set on every new session cookie, not just the first one
tests.executable:
import tempfile, os
from flaskr import create_app

def test_session_cookie_httponly_persists_after_logout_and_re_login():
    fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp()
    os.close(fd)
    app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
    with app.app_context():
        from flaskr.db import init_db
        init_db()
    client = app.test_client()
    r1 = client.post('/auth/login', data={'username': 'Ishaan', 'password': 'stone'})
    assert r1.status_code == 302
    sc1 = r1.headers.get('Set-Cookie', '')
    assert sc1 != '', 'Set-Cookie must be present on first login'
    d1 = [d.strip().lower() for d in sc1.split(';')]
    assert 'httponly' in d1, f'HttpOnly missing on first login: {sc1}'
    r_out = client.get('/auth/logout')
    assert r_out.status_code == 302
    r2 = client.post('/auth/login', data={'username': 'Ishaan', 'password': 'stone'})
    assert r2.status_code == 302
    sc2 = r2.headers.get('Set-Cookie', '')
    assert sc2 != '', 'Set-Cookie must be present on second login'
    d2 = [d.strip().lower() for d in sc2.split(';')]
    assert 'httponly' in d2, f'HttpOnly missing on second login: {sc2}'

test_session_cookie_httponly_persists_after_logout_and_re_login()

tests.name: test_failed_login_does_not_set_httponly_session_cookie
preconditions: App is created with TESTING=True and a fresh temp database
User 'Diya' exists but wrong password is supplied
actions: POST /auth/login with username=Diya and incorrect password 'wrongpass'
Inspect response status and Set-Cookie header
expected: Response status code is 200 (re-renders login form, no redirect)
No session cookie with HttpOnly is set (session was not established)
trace: R-FLASKR-043: HttpOnly session cookie must only be issued on successful authentication, not on failed login
tests.executable:
import tempfile, os
from flaskr import create_app

def test_failed_login_does_not_set_httponly_session_cookie():
    fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp()
    os.close(fd)
    app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
    with app.app_context():
        from flaskr.db import init_db
        init_db()
    client = app.test_client()
    r = client.post('/auth/login', data={'username': 'Diya', 'password': 'wrongpass'})
    assert r.status_code == 200
    assert b'Incorrect password.' in r.data
    set_cookie = r.headers.get('Set-Cookie', '')
    if set_cookie:
        directives = [d.strip().lower() for d in set_cookie.split(';')]
        assert 'httponly' not in directives, (
            f'HttpOnly session cookie must not be set on failed login: {set_cookie}'
        )

test_failed_login_does_not_set_httponly_session_cookie()
